finding.claim: dropTable ignores the return value of Authorize(u, "dba"), so any authenticated user (any role) can reach the DROP TABLE statement on /admin/drop.
finding.source: Any authenticated user's request to POST/GET /admin/drop (no role required; the role check's error is discarded)
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27, a destructive schema operation

trace.note: /admin/drop routed to dropTable with no authorization middleware in this file
u := userFrom(r) loads the authenticated user from request context
Authorize(u, "dba") called as a bare statement; its error (forbidden) is discarded
Execution continues unconditionally to runSQL with the DROP TABLE statement
Authorize returns errors.New("forbidden") for non-dba users, so the discarded result is exactly the non-dba case

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) correctly denies non-dba users, but its result is not used at api.go:26. No other check between api.go:25 and api.go:27. No route-level middleware visible in api.go:44-45. The correct pattern is present in vacuum (api.go:33-36), which is the contrast. Not a decoy: matches case 01-perm-result-ignored exactly. Caveat: the upstream middleware that sets the "user" context value (api.go:22) is not in this directory; if it enforces authentication it only limits callers to logged-in users, not dba role.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error for non-dba users, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at api.go:26 and discards the result. No other check sits between userFrom (api.go:25) and runSQL (api.go:27). No route middleware is registered for /admin/drop (api.go:44). The only visible context-setting code is userFrom (api.go:22), which reads a "user" value and does not enforce a role. The vacuum handler (api.go:33-36) checks the error correctly, so the flaw is specific to dropTable.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: /admin/drop routes to dropTable (api.go:44), Authorize's error is discarded at api.go:26, and execution reaches runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 for any caller whose context carries a user. The only remaining uncertainty is upstream middleware outside this directory, which at most limits callers to authenticated users and does not block a non-dba user here, so the finding stands. The concatenated table name is also a SQL injection path.

finding.claim: The table name parameter r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into raw SQL text, giving SQL injection (and arbitrary statement injection where the driver allows multiple statements) in the DROP TABLE path.
finding.source: HTTP form parameter "t" (r.FormValue) at api.go:27, attacker-controlled
finding.sink: runSQL(string) at api.go:27 (stub at api.go:41; executes SQL text)

trace.note: runSQL receives the built string; the stub does not show parameterization, and a DROP TABLE identifier cannot be bound as a parameter anyway

finding.guards_checked: No identifier allowlist, quoting, or validation on "t" before concatenation at api.go:27. Not a decoy: matches case 10-sql-concat pattern. Reachability depends on F1 (any authenticated user, since the dba check is discarded). runSQL body is a stub in this repo, so the exact driver behavior (multi-statement support) is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error return is discarded, so the dba check never blocks. No allowlist, quoting, or validation of r.FormValue("t") before concatenation at api.go:27. The only real check, at api.go:33-35 in vacuum, is absent from dropTable.
verdict.reason: Route /admin/drop (api.go:44) passes r.FormValue("t") (api.go:27) unvalidated into "DROP TABLE " + value, and the Authorize result at api.go:26 is discarded, so any authenticated user reaches the sink. The runSQL body is a stub at api.go:41, so whether the driver accepts multiple statements is unverified; the concatenation and the authorization bypass are confirmed from the code alone.
